stories.headline: Lithuania charges 13 suspects in Russia GRU-linked assassination plots targeting activist and Russian dissident
stories.summary: Lithuanian authorities announced charges against 13 people from multiple countries in connection with two attempted murders in Vilnius linked to Russia's GRU military intelligence. The targets were a Lithuanian fundraiser for Ukraine and a Russian opposition figure from Bashkortostan who had received political asylum in Lithuania; nine suspects were arrested in Lithuania and abroad.

stories.headline: Nausėda backs joining US freedom of navigation coalition in Strait of Hormuz, to present to defence council
stories.summary: President Nausėda publicly confirmed Lithuania received a US invitation to join a coalition aimed at restoring safe shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, and expressed personal support, framing it as solidarity with allies and a reciprocal obligation. He said the proposal would be presented to Lithuania's defence council for formal consideration.

stories.headline: Ruginienė travels to Yerevan for EPC Summit, meets Armenian PM Pashinyan
stories.summary: Prime Minister Ruginienė conducted a two-day working visit to Yerevan for the 8th European Political Community summit (May 3–4), meeting Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan to discuss bilateral relations, regional security, and Armenia–EU cooperation. She also attended the Armenian Genocide memorial complex and met the local Lithuanian community.

stories.headline: LSDP congress elects Sinkevičius as permanent chairman; extends leadership mandate to four years
stories.summary: The Lithuanian Social Democratic Party (LSDP) held its congress in Jonava on May 1–2, electing Mindaugas Sinkevičius—the Jonava mayor who had served as acting chair—as permanent party chairman with 503 of 535 delegate votes. The congress also approved statute changes extending the leadership mandate from two to four years, passed a resolution on demographic policy, and featured speeches touching on internal party challenges and the Paluckas investigation.

stories.headline: Media and commentators sustain intense scrutiny of Ruginienė's competence and communications style following contentious interview
stories.summary: A wave of Lithuanian media commentary, expert analysis, and satirical content targeted Prime Minister Ruginienė's leadership competence following a tense televised interview with journalist Rima Urbonaitė; a communications expert published analyses arguing her evasiveness is strategic rather than accidental, a satirical song by journalist Andrius Tapinas went viral, and veteran politician Irena Degutienė and former PM's party honorary chairman Vytenis Andriukaitis publicly acknowledged her weaknesses.

stories.summary: President Nausėda signed into law Seimas-approved legislation establishing a new military training ground in Kapčiamiestis—strategic for the Suwałki Corridor and national division formation—and expanding the existing Tauragė training range; he proposed naming the new ground after 19th-century uprising figure Emilija Pliaterytė.

stories.summary: Former Seimas member Kazys Starkevičius—implicated in a Plant and Food Products Agency corruption case—admitted taking a bribe of up to €20,000 and resigned his seat and party membership; former TS-LKD chairman Gabrielius Landsbergis publicly demanded the party immediately sever all ties with Starkevičius, and commentators alleged the scheme was not isolated.

stories.headline: Landsbergis publicly questions TS-LKD's strategic direction; defends Greece property acquisition amid controversy
stories.summary: Former TS-LKD chairman Gabrielius Landsbergis stated publicly he no longer fully understands the current direction of the party led by Laurynas Kasčiūnas, prompting a rebuttal from Kasčiūnas who said the party is consistently moving rightward. Separately, Landsbergis responded to public speculation about his family's property purchase in Greece, saying his family is prepared to defend Lithuania.

stories.headline: Ruginienė and Nausėda publicly disagree on approach to pension system reform and mandatory annuities
stories.summary: Following mass withdrawals from the second pillar pension fund and Nausėda's public proposal to abolish mandatory annuities, Prime Minister Ruginienė rejected the president's approach, arguing the government had chosen a 'more precise' method to increase pensions; the dispute continued through the week with analysis pieces and commentary on the structural implications for Sodra.

stories.headline: LRT public broadcaster law amendments and Venice Commission referral trigger political dispute
stories.summary: Governing LSDP-initiated amendments to the LRT law drew opposition from media figures and the LRT director; PM Ruginienė praised the Seimas Culture Committee's decision to await Venice Commission conclusions before advancing the bill, while LSDP honorary chairman Andriukaitis defended the amendments. A separately-discovered spy pen at a closed LSDP council session added to tensions around media-political relations.

stories.headline: Stabbing attack at Marijampolė school prompts Ruginienė to call for strengthening security in educational institutions
stories.summary: A 17-year-old student injured three schoolmates with a knife at the Sūduva gymnasium in Marijampolė; PM Ruginienė responded publicly, stating school security cannot be taken for granted and requires collective attention.

stories.headline: Former PM Paluckas under criminal investigation; immunity lift request prompts political reactions
stories.summary: Prosecutor General Nida Grunskienė sent a request to the Seimas seeking to lift the parliamentary immunity of former PM and LSDP figure Gintautas Paluckas, who is under criminal investigation; PM Ruginienė called it appropriate to let law enforcement proceed, and new LSDP chair Sinkevičius said Paluckas is free to decide his own political future.

stories.headline: Nausėda expresses conditional support for EU joint army concept within NATO framework
stories.summary: President Nausėda said he would support the idea of a joint EU army if it were framed as increasing Europe's contribution to NATO rather than as an alternative to the alliance, speaking on LRT television.

stories.headline: Bank of Lithuania proposes reform of investment life insurance agent compensation to address consumer harm
stories.summary: The Bank of Lithuania called on the Seimas to amend insurance law to restrict agent commissions tied directly to product sales, citing conflicts of interest in the investment life insurance market where commissions can reach €770 per contract—nearly four times EU averages; the Finance Ministry indicated it would bring changes.

stories.headline: Bank of Lithuania joins Latvia–OECD financial literacy campaign against digital fraud
stories.summary: As part of an EU-funded Technical Support Instrument project, the Bank of Lithuania and Latvijas Banka are jointly developing an action plan to strengthen digital financial literacy and resilience against fraud among Baltic residents, following an April 24 workshop presenting data on the current state of financial fraud.
